items.stem: A company reports a current ratio of 2.5 and a quick (acid-test) ratio of 0.8. What does the gap between these two ratios most strongly indicate?

options.text: A large proportion of current assets is tied up in inventory
options.rationale: Correct: the quick ratio excludes inventory, so a current ratio far above the quick ratio means inventory is a large part of current assets.

options.text: The company has no current liabilities
options.rationale: Both ratios use current liabilities as the denominator; the gap is driven by the numerator, not by having no current liabilities.

options.text: Receivables are being collected faster than average
options.rationale: Collection speed is measured by receivables days, not by the gap between current and quick ratios.
A quick ratio below 1 is a liquidity concern but does not by itself establish insolvency.

items.explanation: Correct: the quick ratio excludes inventory, so a current ratio far above the quick ratio means inventory is a large part of current assets.

items.stem: A firm can raise debt at an after-tax cost of 6% and equity at a cost of 12%. Its target capital structure is 40% debt and 60% equity. What is its weighted average cost of capital (WACC)?

options.rationale: This is the simple average of 6% and 12%, which ignores the 40/60 weights.
This adds the two costs; WACC is a weighted average, not a sum.
This is only the equity component (0.60 x 12%); the debt component must be added.

items.stem: Select TWO costs that are relevant to a short-term decision on whether to accept a one-off special order.

options.text: Incremental variable costs of producing the order
options.rationale: Correct: additional variable costs caused by the order are relevant.

options.text: The contribution forgone on displaced regular sales
options.rationale: Correct: opportunity cost of lost regular sales is a relevant cost.
Depreciation on assets already owned is a sunk, non-cash allocation and is not relevant.
Apportioned fixed overhead that will not change is not relevant to the decision.

options.text: The original purchase price of raw material already in stock
options.rationale: Historic purchase cost is sunk; the relevant measure is the replacement or opportunity cost.

items.explanation: Correct: additional variable costs caused by the order are relevant.
